text:
markdown-docx 0.3.14 syntax

Supported Markdown:
  ATX and Setext headings, paragraphs, emphasis, strong text, strikethrough, superscript, subscript, inline code, hard line breaks, fenced code blocks with syntax coloring for recognized language labels, plus plain indented code blocks, blockquotes, thematic breaks, ordered and unordered lists, task lists, pipe tables, links, and images.

Links use [link text](https://example.com) or bare URLs and become native Word hyperlinks. Labels preserve inline formatting and optional titles become tooltips. Reference links, angle-bracket autolinks, mailto links, relative file links, and linked inline images are supported wherever their content is allowed. Relative file links resolve from the output document. Destinations are not fetched. Empty link destinations keep the formatted label as ordinary text without a hyperlink. Every heading creates a bookmark. Link to its slug with `[Details](#details)`, including before the heading. Slugs use plain heading text and image labels, normalized to NFC and lowercase. Punctuation is removed except underscores and hyphens. Whitespace becomes a hyphen. Empty slugs use `section`. Duplicates receive `-1`, `-2`, and later available suffixes in document order. Unicode and percent-encoded fragments are supported. Fragments must match the slug exactly. Missing targets produce `internal_link_unresolved` with the source line. Word bookmark names are generated separately to fit Word constraints.

Inline syntax: ~~text~~ is strikethrough, x^2^ is superscript, and H~2~O is subscript.

Lists: the first ordered marker sets the starting number, including zero. Later markers do not reset numbering. Separate lists restart independently. Nested lists have independent sequences. Indented continuation paragraphs are unnumbered and aligned with item text. Items may contain headings, code blocks, quotes, tables, and images. Nested blocks retain source order and align with item text. Task markers `- [ ]` and `- [x]` at the start of a list item become clickable Word check boxes. Ordered task items retain their number. Task items can mix with ordinary list items and contain rich nested content. Empty list items create blank numbered or bulleted Word paragraphs. Mapped list styles must reference native template numbering.

Blockquotes may contain paragraphs, headings, lists, code blocks, tables, images, and nested blockquotes. Nested blocks keep their own editable Word styles and gain quote indentation. A lone `>` creates an empty Quote paragraph.

Footnotes use the named `[^label]` and `[^label]: note text` extension from mdit-py-plugins. Labels are case-sensitive. Forward references, formatted text, links, hard breaks, and multiple note paragraphs are supported. Indent later paragraphs by four spaces. Each label must be defined and referenced exactly once. Empty notes are allowed. Undefined labels, duplicate definitions, unused definitions, and repeated references produce line-aware errors. Notes cannot contain images, lists, tables, headings, code blocks, metadata, or nested notes. References in image labels are rejected. References render as native Word notes with automatic numbering. No custom directive is required.

Pipe-table header rows repeat automatically when a table spans pages in Word. Body rows are not marked as headers. No Markdown directive is required. The underlying library exposes `row.repeat_as_header` for callers that need explicit control.

Thematic breaks create empty Word paragraphs with bottom borders, matching Word's horizontal-line shortcut. Ordinary HTML comments are ignored. Raw HTML tags and blocks remain unsupported. Fenced code uses the first info-string word as a Pygments lexer alias. Recognized languages use the Pygments default light style as editable Word run colors and emphasis. Unknown or missing labels and indented code remain plain. Spaces, tabs, and internal blank lines are preserved.

Images: alt text becomes the Word image description. Optional Markdown image titles become image titles. Standalone, inline, and linked images support both. Formatting markers in alt text are removed while their text is preserved. Empty descriptions stay empty without marking images as decorative.

Templates: --template accepts blank, macro-free .docx or .dotx formatting templates. DOTX input produces a real DOCX output and preserves the source. Populated headers and footers remain unsupported.

Metadata comments:
  document metadata must be first
  section metadata starts a next-page section
  <!-- markdown-docx: page-break --> inserts a page break
  table metadata must immediately precede a pipe table
  image metadata must immediately precede a standalone image

Fonts: document.fonts.body and document.fonts.headings set Latin theme fonts. Mapped styles inherit from those theme slots. Omitted overrides preserve template settings. document.fonts.monospace stays explicit for code. Fonts are not embedded or installed.

Lengths use in, cm, mm, or pt. Image widths may also use percentages.

Unsupported in 0.3.14:
  raw HTML tags and blocks, macro-enabled DOCM and DOTM templates, floating images, headers and footers from Markdown, page-number fields, and direct OOXML features.

fonts.body: nonempty font name for the minor Latin theme font
fonts.headings: nonempty font name for the major Latin theme font
fonts.monospace: nonempty fixed font name for code, default Consolas
